skill.name: doc-generator
skill.description: Generate markdown documentation from Python codebases by analyzing source files, extracting docstrings, type hints, and code structure. Use when the user asks to document Python code, create API docs, or generate README files from source code.
skill.summary: Generate Markdown API documentation from Python source files.
skill.author: bossjones

security_audit.summary: The eight static backtick findings are false positives from Markdown code fences and inline identifiers, not shell or Ruby execution. One contextual issue remains: the skill recommends runtime introspection with inspect, which can require importing target Python modules and executing top-level code. The author should prefer AST parsing and require sandboxing or explicit confirmation for runtime inspection.

remediation.issue: Runtime introspection can execute untrusted Python during documentation generation.
remediation.suggestion: Use ast parsing by default. Only use inspect after explicit user confirmation and inside a sandboxed environment.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 29 opens a Markdown example block with triple backticks. It is documentation formatting, not Ruby or shell command execution.
Line 41 shows an inline Markdown method signature example. The backticks quote display text and do not execute commands.
Line 50 uses inline Markdown formatting for a parameter name. There is no shell, Ruby, or command invocation context.
Line 57 opens a fenced Python example inside the documented output format. It is static documentation text, not executable code.
Line 59 closes the fenced Python example. The marker is Markdown syntax and contains no executable command.
Line 60 closes the larger Markdown example block. This is output-format documentation, not a runtime execution instruction.
Line 85 names the Python ast module using inline Markdown code formatting. Referencing a module name is not command execution.
Line 86 names the Python inspect module using inline Markdown code formatting. The backticks are presentational and do not execute shell or Ruby code.

semantic_findings.title: Potential Unsafe Runtime Introspection
semantic_findings.description: The skill recommends Python inspection for runtime introspection. Inspecting untrusted Python modules can require importing them, which may execute top-level code during documentation generation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guidance explicitly allows inspection and names inspect for runtime introspection. Confidence is moderate because it does not explicitly instruct imports, but runtime inspection commonly requires loading target modules.

content.value_statement: Python projects often lack current API documentation. This skill helps Claude, Codex, or Claude Code create Markdown docs from source structure, docstrings, and type hints.
actual_capabilities: Generates Markdown documentation for Python files and directories.
Extracts module, class, function, and method docstrings.
Includes type hints in signatures when they are present.
Organizes API references into modules, classes, methods, and functions.
Adds tables of contents for larger modules.
Handles missing docstrings and syntax errors with warnings.
limitations: It is focused on Python codebases and Markdown output.
Generated descriptions depend on available docstrings and source clarity.
Runtime inspection can be unsafe for untrusted code unless sandboxed.
It does not define a full documentation site build system.

use_cases.title: Document a Python Package
use_cases.description: Create a structured Markdown API reference from package modules, classes, methods, and functions.

use_cases.title: Refresh a Project README
use_cases.description: Generate README sections that summarize public APIs, usage examples, and available type signatures.

use_cases.title: Prepare Internal API Notes
use_cases.description: Turn service or utility modules into readable documentation for handoff, onboarding, or review.

prompt_templates.title: Document One File
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single Python file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate Markdown documentation for this Python file. Include the module summary, public classes, public functions, parameters, return values, and clear warnings for missing docstrings.

prompt_templates.title: Create Package API Docs
prompt_templates.scenario: Document a directory of Python modules.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate API documentation for this Python package. Process public modules, group output by module, include class and function signatures, and add a table of contents.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Existing Docs
prompt_templates.scenario: Use existing documentation as a base.
prompt_templates.prompt: Update the existing Markdown documentation using the current Python source. Preserve the current structure where possible, refresh stale signatures, and note undocumented public members.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Documentation Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Python codebase for documentation coverage. Generate Markdown API docs, identify missing or weak docstrings, and recommend the highest priority documentation fixes.

output_examples.input: A user points the skill at a Python module with public classes, methods, and docstrings.
output_examples.output: A Markdown API reference with a module summary, class sections, method signatures, parameter notes, return descriptions, and usage notes.

output_examples.input: A user asks for README content from a small Python package.
output_examples.output: A README-ready section with package overview, public API summary, common usage guidance, and warnings about missing descriptions.

output_examples.input: A user requests documentation coverage for a release branch.
output_examples.output: A documentation report that lists generated sections, missing docstrings, incomplete parameter details, and suggested fixes.

best_practices: Run it on clean source files with current docstrings and type hints.
Prefer AST-based parsing for untrusted repositories.
Review generated examples before publishing them to users.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on generated docs as a substitute for accurate source comments.
Do not use runtime inspection on untrusted Python without isolation.
Do not publish generated API docs without checking public versus private members.

faq.question: What languages does this skill support?
faq.answer: It is designed for Python codebases and Markdown documentation output.

faq.question: Can it generate README files?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create README sections from source structure, docstrings, type hints, and usage examples.

faq.question: Does it require external dependencies?
faq.answer: The skill recommends standard Python tools such as ast, inspect, and pathlib for basic documentation generation.

faq.question: How does it handle missing docstrings?
faq.answer: It continues processing and marks missing descriptions instead of failing the whole documentation task.

faq.question: Is runtime inspection safe?
faq.answer: Runtime inspection can execute target Python code through imports. Use AST parsing or sandbox runtime inspection for untrusted projects.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
